extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, publishers and media organisations (Germany)
extracted.subtask_description: National code of journalistic ethics and procedural rules issued by the German Press Council covering standards for reporting, editorial practice, data protection, advertising separation, corrections and the complaints procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness and preserving human dignity (Section 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the truth, preservation of human dignity and accurate informing of the public are the overriding principles of the Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every person active in the press preserves the standing and credibility of the media; freedom of the press includes independence and freedom of information, the right of expression and criticism, and these must be exercised with responsibility toward the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care (Section 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research is an indispensable instrument of journalistic work; duty of care requires accuracy in researching, editing, publishing, documenting and storing person-related data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abridgements or additions must not distort the sense of a story; publications in word, picture and graphics must be carefully checked in the light of existing circumstances to avoid misleading readers or harming legitimate interests of third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive agreements (Guideline 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The informing of the public about events of general interest must not be restricted or prevented by exclusive agreements with informants or shielding of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who seek a monopoly on information exclude the rest of the press from acquiring important news and thus impinge upon the freedom of information; exclusive agreements that restrict the press are contrary to press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional ethics duty (Guideline 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic principles define professional ethics: maintain the standing of the press and speak up for the freedom of the press; respect editorial data protection rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers, editors and journalists must be aware of their responsibility and duty to uphold the prestige and independence of the press in line with constitutional principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews (Guideline 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A verbatim interview is journalistically correct; if quoted in full or part the publication must state its source; paraphrases should still indicate the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the basic content of verbally expressed thoughts is paraphrased, it is journalistic honour to state the source; publications should correct quoted interviews if they misrepresent what was said.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readers' letters (Guideline 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers' letters may be published to allow opinions not shared by the editorial team, but must be handled according to Press Code: identification, consent, abridgement rules and secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters are normally published with the author's name; addresses should generally be omitted; changes or abridgements are impermissible without consent except when a regular notice states editors may shorten without changing meaning; correspondence is subject to editorial secrecy and must not be passed to third parties; pseudo‑nyms may be retained when user-generated content is used but the source must be indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic photographs and pictorial representations
rubrics_metrics.description: If an illustration could be taken as documentary by a casual reader but is symbolic, it must be clearly marked as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute/auxiliary illustrations, symbolic illustrations (reconstructions, artificially visualised events), photomontages or other changes must be clearly marked in caption or accompanying text to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance reports (Guideline 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press bears full journalistic responsibility for advance reports published in a compressed form; those who further distribute advance reports by stating the source must be able to rely on that source's validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compressed advance reports must be checked; publications must ensure abridgements do not distort basic elements or prompt incorrect conclusions that harm legitimate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion poll findings (Guideline 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing results of opinion polls the press shall give the number of respondents, the date of the poll, the identity of the person or organisation that commissioned it, and the questions asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether the institute was commissioned; indicate representativeness; if institute implemented poll on its own initiative this should be pointed out; exclude poll results from graphical representations when not representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic representations (Guideline 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of care requires misleading distortions be avoided in graphic representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphs and infographics must not create a false impression; data and visual scales must accurately represent underlying facts and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases (Guideline 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must be identified as such if they are published by the editorial team without further editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial teams should mark press releases clearly so readers can distinguish paid or external material from independent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-generated content (Guideline 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press bears responsibility for all its publications, including user-generated content; such content must be clearly marked as user-generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors shall ensure compliance with journalistic principles and act if they detect violations in user content; when taking over user-generated content as readers' letters, source/pseudonym must be indicated; publication of fake readers' letters is incompatible with duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections — requirements (Guideline 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published news or assertions that turn out to be incorrect must be promptly rectified in an appropriate manner by the publication concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reader must be able to recognise the previous article was wholly or partly incorrect; corrections must refer to the incorrect article and publish the true facts even if the error was admitted elsewhere; online rectifications should be linked to the original content and marked as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections — documentation (Guideline 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If editorial research or use of person-related data results in corrections, retractions or reprimands, the publication must store them with the original data and document them for the same period as the original data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of corrections and associated material for accountability and potential complaints handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of research (Guideline 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must identify themselves as such; untrue statements about identity are fundamentally irreconcilable with the press; undercover research may be justifiable only in individual cases for information of particular public interest that cannot be obtained by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accidents and disasters, emergency services have priority over the public right to information; undercover research requires careful justification and must respect ethical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research among people requiring protection (Guideline 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting research among people requiring protection (vulnerable persons, children, those emotionally affected), particular restraint is required and limited willpower must not be exploited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid aggressive or manipulative methods; adapt approach to protect dignity and wellbeing of vulnerable interviewees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and data transfer (Guideline 4.3 / Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: All person-related data gathered, processed and used for journalistic-editorial purposes are subject to editorial secrecy; transfer between editorial departments is permissible but must be annotated and restricted to journalistic-editorial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal data gathered in violation of the Press Code are to be blocked or deleted by the publication; transfer should be documented and handled only for editorial purposes; confidentiality should be respected and informant identities not revealed without permission except in narrowly defined cases (serious crime/duty to inform police).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of dishonest newsgathering and secret service activities (Guidelines 5.1 & 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dishonest methods must not be used to acquire person-related news, information or photographs; secret service activities by journalists and publishers are irreconcilable with professional secrecy and prestige of the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must refuse inducements or deceitful practices; avoid operations indistinguishable from intelligence work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional secrecy and confidentiality (Section 5 / Guideline 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press shall respect professional secrecy, use the right to refuse to bear witness and not reveal informants' identities without explicit permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality is to be adhered to in principle; exceptions only in narrowly defined legal/ethical circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of activities / dual functions (Guideline 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and publishers shall not perform any activities that could throw doubt over the credibility of the press; dual functions (e.g., public office, business roles) must be strictly separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a journalist exercises another function, compliance with journalistic principles must be ensured from the outset and potential conflicts disclosed or avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of advertising and editorial content (Section 7 / Guideline 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial publications must not be influenced by private or business interests; paid publications must be so designed that the reader can recognise advertising as such and be separable by identification and/or design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations under advertising law apply; if a publication concerns the publisher's own interests this must be clearly identifiable to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrpetitious advertising (Guideline 7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial stories about companies, products or services must not overstep the boundary to surreptitious advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary when content is paid for or influenced by third parties; highlight sponsored content and avoid covert promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special publications (Guideline 7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial special publications are subject to the same editorial responsibility as all other editorial content; advertising special publications must respect editorial requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special issues or supplements must still comply with Press Code principles and clearly differentiate advertising from editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of private locations (Guideline 7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Private addresses and other private locations (hospitals, care facilities, rehabilitation centres) enjoy special protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should refrain from publishing private addresses or locations unless justified by public interest and consent; take extra care with sensitive locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of names/identifying info of suspects/perpetrators (Guideline 8.1 & 8.3 parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press shall only publish names, photographs and other information enabling identification of suspects or perpetrators if the legitimate interest of the public outweighs the interests worthy of protection of the persons involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider include intensity of suspicion, seriousness of allegation, state of proceedings, fame of suspect, earlier behaviour and the intensity of seeking public office/mandate; sensational interests alone do not justify identifying reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of victims and witnesses (Guideline 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Victims have the right to special protection; publication of names or photographs of witnesses is generally inadmissible; reporting on suicide calls for restraint regarding names, photographs, and circumstance descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain consent of victims/relatives before identifying; treat victims with particular sensitivity to avoid further harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children and young people (Guideline 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reporting on crimes and accidents, identification of children and young people is inadmissible before completion of their 18th year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule avoid names, photos or other identifying information for minors; exercise special restraint given their future prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing persons (Guideline 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and photographs of missing persons may be published, however only in agreement with the responsible authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with authorities to avoid endangering searches or relatives; ensure publication serves the search and public safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illnesses and injuries (Guideline 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical and mental illnesses or injuries are part of a person's private sphere; as a rule the press should refrain from reporting about illnesses or injuries without the consent of the affected persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only report medical information when relevant to public interest and with appropriate consent or anonymisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and financial market reporting (Guideline 8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and publishers shall not buy or sell securities — directly or through agents — on which they have published, plan to report, or have reported in the previous two weeks, with intent of enriching themselves or close persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use privileged editorial information for financial gain; avoid conflicts of interest in market coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anniversary dates (Guideline 8.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of anniversary dates of persons who are otherwise not in the public eye requires that the editorial department confirms in advance whether those involved consent to the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check consent for retrospective or commemorative articles about private individuals; treat such publications as potentially intrusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information rights of affected persons (Guideline 8.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a press report has a negative effect on someone’s personal rights, on request the affected person must be given information about the respective personal data stored by the responsible publication organ; information may be declined in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access to stored data unless it risks revealing informants, contributors, guarantors or would otherwise conflict with legitimate reasons to decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on reporting (Guideline 13.2 / related)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the press has reported on an unconfirmed conviction of a person, it should also report an ensuing acquittal or a marked lessening of charges if the legitimate interests of the person affected do not dictate otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure corrective follow-up reporting to mitigate harm from earlier inaccurate or incomplete reporting; publicize acquittals to maintain fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensational reporting and protection of young people (Section 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press shall refrain from inappropriately sensational portrayal of violence, brutality and suffering and shall respect protection of young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gruesome front-page depictions and sensational language that reduce persons to objects; consider effects on children and young people when placing pictorial representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on crimes — general duties (Section 8 / Guideline 8.1-8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on investigations, proceedings and trials must inform the public carefully and must not prejudge persons; the principle of presumption of innocence applies to press coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use media as a 'pillory' to punish socially; report independently and authentically, distinguishing between suspicion and proven guilt; consider resocialisation interests when reporting on past proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal reporting — special categories (Guideline 13.3 & 13.6 parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on young persons, special restraint is necessary considering future prospects; reports should not prejudice outcome or use reporting to punish beyond judicial sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid naming young defendants; focus on public interest and avoid sensationalising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminals' memoirs (Guideline 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of so-called criminals' memoirs infringes journalistic principles if crimes are justified or qualified with hindsight; such publications may satisfy demand for sensation and are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise editorial judgement; avoid publishing material that glamorises or justifies criminal acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and escape reporting (Guideline 11.2 & 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In countries where opposition to the government can mean danger, the press must consider whether publishing names or photographs will endanger persecuted people; reports on escapees and their routes must not endanger relatives or close persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess safety risks to subjects and third parties before publishing identifying information; weigh public interest against potential harm or closure of escape routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting acts of violence (Guideline 11.1 / 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reporting actual and threatened acts of violence, the press should weigh public interest against interests of the victims and others; reporting should be independent and authentic but not a tool for criminals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensational details that could glorify violence; maintain distinction between verified facts and speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of dignity (Section 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating people's dignity with inappropriate representations in word and image contradicts journalistic ethics; persons should not be reduced to objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the humanity of subjects in reporting and imagery; avoid humiliating or demeaning portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accidents and disasters reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The limit of acceptability in reports on accidents and disasters is respect for the suffering of the victims and their dependants; victims must not suffer a second time by media portrayal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to emergency services; avoid intrusive reporting at scenes and sensational depiction of victims' suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination (Section 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no discrimination against a person because of sex, disability or membership of an ethnic, religious, social or national group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reporting that fosters prejudices or generalisations about groups; mention group membership only when legitimately relevant to the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical reporting (Section 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports on medical matters should not be sensationalist; preliminary research must not be portrayed as conclusive or almost conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating unfounded hopes or fears; characterise research findings by stage and limitations; seek expert verification where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential treatment / invitations and gifts (Guideline 15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of privileges that could influence freedom of decision of a publishing house or editorial staff should be avoided; invitations or gifts exceeding normal business value must not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-value advertising articles or small objects are harmless; journalists must insist information be given regardless of gifts; reveal financing when reporting on press trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of public reprimands (Section 16 / Guideline 16.1-16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a public reprimand is issued by the German Press Council it must be published by the publication concerned; the reader must be informed of the facts of the reprimanded article and of the journalistic principle the article violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprimands must be published in an appropriate form and in telecommunications media be linked to the reprimanded contribution; editors may refrain from further publication after 30 days if they have modified the contribution as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to complain to the German Press Council (Complaints Procedure Section 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may complain to the German Press Council about publications or proceedings in German press undertakings and telecommunications media with journalistic and editorial contents; complaints about data protection are handled by the Complaints Committee on Editorial Data Protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints should be made in writing (post or e-mail); anonymous or obviously abusive complaints are not dealt with; time limits generally apply (usually within one year from first publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of complaints (Section 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every complaint must be in writing, state a reason, and include the original or a copy of the relevant publication or, for online items, a screenshot/printout with date and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints should include links/prints with timestamps; in data protection cases timing is based on when complainant became aware of the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior scrutiny of complaints (Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a prior scrutiny to determine whether the German Press Council is responsible; the Council shall reject undecided or obviously unjustified complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected, the complainant may appeal within two weeks; prior scrutiny prevents handling of irrelevant or abusive complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of the respondent (Section 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall be informed and given opportunity to reply; Complaints Committees invite members and can request statements and supplementary conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents typically have three weeks to make a statement; their remedial actions are considered when assessing appropriate rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman's decision (Section 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chairman of the Complaints Committee may reject complaints as unjustified or decide to launch proceedings; the Chair can instigate preparatory actions and may rule even in the absence of invited parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair's decisions include reasons and list invited witnesses; parties are informed of key reasons for Chairman's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of impartiality and mediation (Section 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may be challenged for presumed partiality; the Press Council may mediate between parties and suspend processing during mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for rejection must be in writing and justified; if mediation succeeds the complaints procedure ends; deadlines are deferred during mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparations and hearings (Sections 8 & 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints Committees prepare hearings by inviting parties and witnesses; hearings are not open to the public, chaired by the chairman, recorded and documented, and produce a written, signed ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations sent at least four weeks before meeting; invited parties must confirm attendance two weeks prior; a record is produced and any petitions appended as annexes; final ruling sent within three weeks after hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulings — grounds and possible outcomes (Section 12 & 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complaint is justified, the committee may issue an advice notice, a disapproval or a reprimand; in weighing whether to issue a reprimand the adjudicating body takes account of gravity, consequences and remedial steps taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final written ruling must be justified and signed; committees may waive action in certain cases even if complaint is justified; decisions consider both individual and general press-ethical interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations and advice notices (Section 11 Complaints Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice notices and recommendations capable of clarifying a situation or producing amicable agreement may be issued at any stage of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notices are intended to rectify situations or encourage corrective measures without formal reprimand; they may be used where resocialisation or privacy interests advise against publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to publish reprimands (Section 15 Complaints Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprimands must be published in the publications or telecommunications media concerned in an appropriate form; publication may be waived to protect interests of an affected person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In telemedia the reprimand should be linked to the contribution when it is called up; after 30 days editors may refrain from further publication if content has been modified according to the reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of proceedings (Section 14 Complaints Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members and employees of the German Press Council must maintain confidentiality concerning discussions and documents; prior to delivering a ruling they may issue only formal statements not indicating voting intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality preserves integrity of deliberations; public communications should be limited to formal status until ruling is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of proceedings (Section 16 Complaints Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed complaints procedure is revisable by resumption if new circumstances are proven that would justify a significantly different decision or if relevant aspects were not communicated or considered in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resumption may be requested immediately by complainant/respondent or initiated by committee if new evidence or omissions surface; in case of change in adjudicatory practice only advice notices may be issued.
